messages.subject: Re: STAR output to featureCount-resorting
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ji,

I ran STAR (v2.6.0c) on the "BAM Unsorted" mode to map a paired-end sample, then used featureCounts (v1.6.2) on the mapping results. No "reads from the same pair were found not adjacent" message was reported.

I then ran STAR on the "BAM SortedByCoordinate" mode to map the same paired-end sample, and featureCounts reported the "reads from the same pair were found not adjacent" message.

Can you please provide us with your full command line for running STAR and featureCounts?

BTW, the read counting results are identical in the above two runs.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: Re: STAR output to featureCount-resorting
messages.body_plain: You should not use the "−−donotsort" option unless you are absolutely sure that both reads from a pair are present in your bam file and they are next to each other in the bam file. If this is not the case, reads from different pairs might be treated as being from the same pair and then incorrectly counted.

messages.subject: featureCounts numOfBuckets error
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I was hoping you could help me. I am running featureCounts on some metagenomics data using a custom GTF file (~4Gb in size) and large BAM mappings to contigs (each BAM is around 12Gb and there are 16 BAMs).
This has run before no problem on a slightly smaller run, so I assumed it might be size related. But the error I am getting suggests otherwise.

featureCounts throws the following error when loading the :

"||    Paired-end reads are included.                                          ||
    ||    Assign alignments to features...                                        ||
    featureCounts: hashtable.c:172: HashTableCreate: Assertion `numOfBuckets > 0' failed."

Any ideas what is going wrong?

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts numOfBuckets error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt,

Although your GTF file is indeed huge, its size shouldn't be a problem for featureCounts. I've just generated a GTF file having 50 million lines and 4GB large, but featureCounts did read assignment with no errors on it. The peak memory use was 5.2GB.

Can you provide more details on:

1) the full command line for running featureCounts.
2) the lines in your GTF file.
3) the amount of meta-features (eg different gene_ids) in your GTF file.
4) the version of featureCounts you are using.
5) the size of your BAM file
6) the Operating System where you run the program.

Also, it is best if you can provide us your GTF file and BAM files, so we can reproduce the error.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: Counting exon+UTR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Subread team,

 What is the best way to calculate gene-level read counts for exon plus 3'UTR? From the manual (v1.6.2), it seems only "exons" are counted by default (-t parameter: "'exon’ by default.")?

 The reason I need to include 3'UTR is that we are using 3'mRNA-Seq kit <https://www.lexogen.com/quantseq-3mrna-sequencing/> from Lexogen which a lot of reads are aligned on UTR region.

 By reading the manual, it looks like these three parameters are related:

1. -g (GTF.attrType). ‘gene id’ by default. I will use gene-level counts, so I think I should keep it as default.

2. -t (GTF.featureType). It says "Only rows which have the matched feature type in the provided GTF annotation ﬁle will be included for read counting. ‘exon’ by default.". Do I need o change this?

3. −−extraAttributes (GTF.attrType.extra). It looks like I need to specify "three_prime_utr" for this parameter?

The GTF file I use is from Ensembl Plant maize.

The code I used for now is "featureCounts -T 4 -a maize.gtf -o output input.bam".

 Any suggestions are welcomed.

 Thanks for your time.

Best,
Ji

messages.subject: Re: Counting exon+UTR
messages.body_plain:
3' UTR region is normally included as part of the last exon of a gene so it is likely that your 3UTR counts are already included in the counts generated for the last exons. This also means that the 3UTR counts have also already been included in your gene-level counts.

The '−−extraAttributes' option just enables extra GTF attributes to be included in the counting output. It does not count reads for extra features. featureCounts only takes one feature type for counting at a time.
